card.title: Essays and one-act plays — theme, character, moment

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Five essays argue (Jobs on death as life's clarifier, Parker on poverty as lived experience, Haldane on what life requires), three one-act plays compress full drama into one room and one crisis (Trifles' women reading what men miss, A Sunny Morning's bench romance, Refund's satire of schooling). Every answer runs theme → evidence (quoted moment) → technique → writer's purpose.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: answer spine: claim (theme in one line) → moment (quoted scene/line) → technique (device, irony, dialogue) → purpose (what the writer makes you feel/decide)  ·  essay tools: thesis, anecdote, rhetoric · play tools: dialogue, stage business, dramatic irony

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Claims need textual moments — unquoted assertions score thin. Separate the writer from the speaker (Jobs the speaker ≠ Jobs the man; narrators can mislead). One-act analysis stays inside the single setting and timespan; importing other works dilutes.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Daudet's 'Last Lesson' classroom-exit moment (mother's eyes leaving her son — NEB 2024, 5 marks): read gesture as theme (language = identity under occupation). Trifles turns 'trifles' (preserves, stitching) into the murder's evidence — the title is the thesis. Satire (Refund, Parker) argues through exaggeration; answer the target, not just the joke.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Last-Lesson moment answer: claim — M. Hamel's final lesson makes language the homeland; moment — the mother's gaze torn from her son by the order; technique — Daudet freezes a gesture instead of explaining it; purpose — occupation steals even farewells, so the reader feels linguistic loss bodily (NEB 2024, 5-mark pattern).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Theme-hunting flattens texts into morals — examiners reward observed detail over slogans. Author intention is partly unknowable; argue from the text, not biography. One framework cannot fit satire and elegy identically — adjust the lens per genre.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Build any answer from the text outward: list striking moments → cluster them into a theme → name the technique carrying each (irony in Refund's exam-farce, symbolism in Trifles' birdcage, rhetoric in Jobs's three stories) → state the purpose as effect-on-reader. Four moves, any essay or play.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Titles are theses (Trifles, Refund, What is Poverty?). Endings reveal purpose — answer from the last scene backward. Always quote: one short exact line beats a paragraph of paraphrase. Device + effect, never device alone.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2024 (5): Last Lesson exit moment — gesture as meaning (literature bank). NEB 2023 (2): device ID — 'wind whispered' = personification. Essay-theme and play-character questions follow the claim→moment→technique→purpose spine.
